model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (distributable earnings less book-growth retention, net debt zero; engine route)

historical_growth.revenue_basis: Net revenue (NII + non-interest income, US GAAP) FY2023 3,908bn -> FY2026 6,937bn; FY2021 5,162bn. Gross Revenues CAGR 24.6% / 15.0% is rate-inflated and not used.
historical_growth.eps_basis: US GAAP basic EPS JPY 31.00 (FY2023) / 86.88 (FY2021) -> 151.74 (FY2026); 3yr distorted by the FY2023 mark-to-market trough.
historical_growth.equity_basis: US GAAP attributable StockholdersEquity 15,661bn (FY2021) / 15,763bn (FY2023) -> 19,573bn (FY2026), after JPY ~1.9tn of buybacks over FY2022-26 and AOCI swings (+3.46tn at FY2026).
historical_growth.fcf_note: Not meaningful for a bank: OCF swings with deposit and trading-asset flows (FY2024 -1.79tn, FY2025 +1.03tn, FY2026 -3.37tn).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.6% vs EPS 5yr 11.8% and net-revenue 3yr 21.1%: >30% divergence. Earnings have outgrown book because BOJ normalisation raised ROE (rate-driven margin, not balance-sheet growth) and buybacks shrank the share count. The forward path therefore separates the one-off rate step (FY2027) from balance-sheet growth (2-3.5%/yr) rather than extrapolating either CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: SBC-zero market: SBC-adjusted and reported series coincide.

scenario_narratives.base: BOJ policy rate holds around 1.00-1.25%. Domestic deposit margins have repriced, so FY2027 lands at the JPY 2.7tn guide (Q1's JPY 809bn suggests upside, but management's unchanged target implies H2 normalisation: credit costs rising off a low base, deposit competition). After that, earnings grow with a mature Japanese balance sheet plus the Asia platforms (Krungsri, Danamon, Shriram), and cross-shareholding sale gains run off. Morgan Stanley equity-method income grows with US capital markets. ROE settles near 12% against an 8.5% cost of equity, which supports about 1.5x book, not the roughly 2.1x the ADR pays today.
scenario_narratives.bull: Japan reflation sticks. The BOJ goes to 1.5% or more, deposit betas stay low and NII compounds. Household money moving from deposits into NISA products lifts trust, asset-management and securities fees. Morgan Stanley has a strong M&A/underwriting cycle, and Shriram/Asia grow at EM-credit rates. FY2027 beats the guide at JPY 2.9tn, ROE climbs toward 13.5%, and capital returns grow. Even here the stock is only about at fair value, because the price already discounts most of the bull case.
scenario_narratives.bear: The profit surge turns out to be a rate story that partly reverses. A global slowdown stalls or reverses the BOJ. Overseas credit costs (Americas CIB, Asia consumer finance) normalise sharply, foreign-currency funding costs spike, and Morgan Stanley earnings fall at the same time, so earnings drop about 13% from the FY2027 level over two years. The JGB/foreign-bond book takes valuation losses. ROE slips to ~9.5%, barely above the cost of equity, and the market re-rates the stock toward 1.0-1.2x book, as it did through 2016-2023.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on the equity cash it can distribute: post-tax attributable earnings less the book retained to grow the balance sheet, discounted at a JPY cost of equity, with deposits treated as operating funding (net debt zero). The J-GAAP earnings basis is used because MUFG's capital, payout and ROE targets are set on it and the US GAAP line is dominated by mark-to-market swings. The price-to-book cross-check: at a sustainable ROE of r, a bank growing at g is worth (r - g)/(CoE - g) times book, so 12% ROE, 1.5% g and 8.5% CoE support about 1.5x book. The ADR trades at about 2.1x US GAAP book.
key_risks_to_valuation: BOJ rate path: each 25bp is worth roughly JPY 100-200bn of pre-tax domestic NII, so a stall or reversal is the bear case
Credit-cycle turn in overseas lending (Americas CIB, Asia consumer finance) while credit costs are near cyclical lows
Morgan Stanley concentration: ~24% equity-method stake, valued inside the earnings stream; an MS downturn hits earnings and capital together
Earnings-basis risk: J-GAAP FY0/guide figures come from company releases, not a filing extracted in this folder; US GAAP attributable NI was 29% lower in FY2026
Cross-shareholding sale gains inside J-GAAP profit are finite and run off over the plan period
Yen translation for ADR holders: the USD value moves 1:1 with USDJPY (157.83 at valuation)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (MUFG, NYSE) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 14.62-24.26. JPY=X and 8306.T from the same API for the FX parity check.
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts CIK 0000067088 (20-F FY ended 2026-03-31, US GAAP): StockholdersEquity, Goodwill, IntangibleAssetsNetExcludingGoodwill, NetIncomeLoss, ProfitLoss, CommonStockSharesIssued, TreasuryStockCommonShares, PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock, PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock, EquitySecuritiesFvNiGainLoss, IncomeLossFromEquityMethodInvestments, Deposits; research/MUFG/Reports/MUFG_Metrics.csv for history.
data_sources.qualitative: research/MUFG/Reports/MUFG_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): J-GAAP FY0 profit JPY 2.43tn, FY2027 guide JPY 2.7tn, Q1 FY2027 JPY 809.4bn, DPS guide JPY 96, JPY 100bn buyback, Shriram JPY 680bn, Morgan Stanley stake ~23.9-24.1%.

inputs.base_revenue_note: NOT bank revenue. The engine stream is FY0 (year to 31-Mar-2026) J-GAAP profit attributable to owners of parent, JPY 2,430,000m (JPY 2.43tn). Margin 100%, tax 0%, SBC/D&A 0% because the stream is already after tax, provisions, NCI and funding cost; the 'capex' path is the equity retained to grow the balance sheet (retention = growth / ROE).
inputs.sbc_source: Not material / not separately disclosed in the 20-F XBRL (no ShareBasedCompensation tag FY2017-FY2026). Japanese executive stock compensation (BIP trust) is small relative to JPY 2.4tn profit; SBC-zero market, so house and street bases coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 (year to Mar-2026) PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock JPY 500.1bn; FY2025 418.4bn; FY2024 400.1bn; plus a JPY 100bn / 45m-share program through 30-Jun-2026 announced May-2026 (not deducted from the share count -- conservative, ~0.3%). Dividends paid FY2026 JPY 846.7bn (JPY 74/sh declared in the year).
inputs.fx_note: Model JPY -> quote USD at 1/157.83 = 0.006336 USD per JPY (Yahoo JPY=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-03T21:07Z). 1 ADS = 1 ordinary share. Parity check: TSE 8306.T close JPY 3,544 (2026-10-02 06:30Z) / 157.83 = USD 22.45 vs NYSE ADS USD 22.82 (2026-10-02 20:00Z), +1.6% -- within the intraday gap between the Tokyo and New York closes, confirming the 1:1 ratio and the rate direction. The Analysis JSON's 'each ADS representing multiple ordinary shares' is wrong; it is 1:1.
inputs.units_note: Money in JPY millions (matching core_metrics); shares in millions; per-share values in JPY, converted to USD at fx_rate.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z NYSE regular close (Friday); Yahoo chart API
inputs.share_count_basis: Issued 11,867.71m (CommonStockSharesIssued, 20-F FY2026) less treasury 580.14m (TreasuryStockCommonShares) = 11,287.6m outstanding, plus ~1.4m dilution (diluted 11,398.4m vs basic 11,397.0m weighted) = 11,289m. Held flat: buybacks are the distribution mechanism and are inside FCFE.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single JPY cost of equity of 8.5% across scenarios (risk charged once, in the scenario weights): 10y JGB ~2.0% (BOJ policy rate 1.00% since Jun-2026) + beta ~1.15 x 5.5% Japan ERP = ~8.3%, rounded to 8.5% for G-SIB leverage and rate-path sensitivity. Built in the flows' currency (JPY), not the USD quote. Not a WACC: the stream is post-interest, so it is discounted at the cost of equity and no debt is deducted.
inputs.lease_treatment: N/A -- lease costs are inside bank operating expense and therefore inside the post-tax profit stream.
inputs.nci_treatment: Stream is profit attributable to owners of parent (after NCI; US GAAP FY2026 NCI share JPY 155bn), so no NCI bridge deduction. Charged once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank -> residual-income/FCFE family per dcf-methods routing; implemented as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine (house precedent NAB.AX, BMO, HSBC): FCFE = distributable earnings x (1 - retention), retention = balance-sheet growth / ROE, net_debt = 0 because deposits (JPY 260.8tn) are operating funding, not debt. EARNINGS BASIS: J-GAAP profit attributable (FY0 JPY 2.43tn; FY2027 guidance JPY 2.7tn, reaffirmed at Q1 with Q1 actual JPY 809.4bn) rather than the 20-F US GAAP figure (JPY 1,729bn attributable FY2026). Reason: dividends (~40% payout target), buybacks, ROE targets and Basel capital are all run on J-GAAP, and the US GAAP line is dominated by mark-to-market noise -- equity-securities FV gains of +JPY 984bn FY2026, -674bn FY2025, +1,528bn FY2024, plus hedge-accounting mismatches -- giving US GAAP NI of -83 / 382 / 1,326 / 1,267 / 1,729bn over FY2022-26. CAVEAT: the J-GAAP FY0 figure (2.43tn) and guidance come from the Analysis JSON (company releases, May/Aug-2026); no J-GAAP 6-K is extracted in this folder, so they are not tied to a filing line here. MORGAN STANLEY: the ~23.9% equity-method stake (US GAAP equity-method income JPY 871bn FY2026, all investees) is valued inside the earnings stream, NOT added in the bridge -- adding it would double count; its market value (~JPY 9-10tn, roughly a quarter of MUFG's cap) is a cross-check, not an add. Cross-shareholding sale gains inside J-GAAP profit are a run-off source; the base path decelerates FY2028+ partly for that reason. Reported OCF/FCF is meaningless for a bank (FY2026 OCF -JPY 3.37tn) and is not used. DATA ISSUES (for the parser, not fixed here): Metrics.csv Currency column says USD but values are JPY (XBRL mislabel, same class as BILI/FUTU); NetIncome in the CSV is ProfitLoss incl. NCI (FY2026 1,883.9bn vs attributable 1,729.4bn); ShareholdersEquity is total equity incl. NCI (20,840bn vs 19,573bn attributable); Revenue is gross Revenues (11,867bn), not net revenue (NII 3,684 + non-interest income 3,253 = 6,937bn). Multiples at the price: P/B 2.08x on US GAAP attributable BVPS JPY 1,734, P/TBV 2.32x (TBVPS JPY 1,553 after goodwill 567bn + intangibles 1,475bn), forward P/E ~14.8x on the JPY 2.7tn guide.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY0 FCFE = 2,430,000 x (1 - 29% base-year retention) ~ 1,725,000. Bank reported FCF (OCF less capex) is not meaningful and not used; actual FY2026 distributions were 1,346,781 (dividends 846,715 + buybacks 500,066).

bear.growth_rates_note: FY2027 roughly flat at JPY 2.45tn (guide missed as H2 credit costs and bond marks bite), then a global credit turn plus a BOJ stall/reversal: FY2028 -10%, FY2029 -3%, before a slow recovery.
bear.narrative: Rate tailwind reverses and overseas credit costs normalise sharply; ROE falls back toward 9.5%, barely above the cost of equity.

base.growth_rates_note: FY2027 = JPY 2.7tn guidance (reaffirmed at Q1); FY2028 +4% full-year effect of the Jun-2026 hike to 1.00% net of rising credit costs and fading cross-shareholding gains; then balance-sheet growth decaying to 1.5%.
base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Stream is already post-tax distributable earnings.
base.capex_pct_path_note: Retention = balance-sheet/RWA growth (3.5, 3.5, 3, 3, 2.5, 2.5, 2, 2, 2, 1.5%) / incremental J-GAAP ROE 12%. Terminal 12.5% = g 1.5% / ROE 12%, consistent with the Gordon growth. Implied payout 71-88% vs FY2026 actual ~55% (dividends 847bn + buybacks 500bn on 2.43tn) -- the excess is capital MUFG is currently redeploying into Asia M&A (Shriram JPY 680bn).
base.narrative: BOJ normalisation is banked at 1.00% and earnings step up to the JPY 2.7tn guide, then grow with a slow Japanese balance sheet plus Asia; ROE holds ~12%, above an 8.5% cost of equity.

bull.growth_rates_note: FY2027 JPY 2.89tn (Q1 JPY 809bn annualises to 3.2tn; guide beaten), BOJ to 1.5%+ by FY2028, Morgan Stanley earnings strong, Asia platforms compounding.
bull.narrative: Rates keep normalising and deposit betas stay low; ROE climbs to ~13.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear at 25%, above the 15% house default, because the earnings step-up rests on one policy variable (the BOJ rate path, flagged high severity in the Analysis) and on credit costs that are cyclically low. Base at 50%: the FY2027 guide is reaffirmed and Q1 is ahead of it. Bull at 25%, below the 35% default, because it needs several independent things at once (further hikes, low deposit betas, a strong Morgan Stanley cycle, smooth Asia M&A). This matches the house megabank precedent (HSBC, BMO at 25/50/25).
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
